name: Bow Drill for Beads, Wood and Stone
one_liner: Bow drill for beads, wood and stone
observation: Bow drill for beads, wood and stone.
prompt:
Create ONE Tomorrow and Tomorrow research painting. Reference supplies ONLY the established production medium/palette and EXACT EXTRA-WIDE CANVAS: preserve its width and aspect, full bleed, no frame/text/grid/3:2. NEW SUBJECT: ONE kneeling craftsperson with EXACTLY TWO hands uses a crude bow drill to bore a small wooden piece. Upper hand presses a palm-sized stone socket on a vertical wooden spindle; other hand moves the curved branch bow horizontally, its coarse cord wound once around spindle. Workpiece supported on low stone. No fire needed. Flat angular palette-knife copper/ember/soot. No metal bit, wheel, carpentry bench, three hands, oversized hunting bow or loose unconnected spindle.
Keep COMPLETE principal heads, hands, tools and mechanism ALL within central y170..590 of a 765px-high banner. Zoom out; top/bottom background only, preserve real 3.37:1 research-card crop. Chronology game years26–28: hide clothing, cordage, baskets, early clay pots, small earthen or hide dwellings, stone and wooden tools. Plain weaving is later, never borrow later technology from style reference.
review: Full extra-wide original and actual 3.37:1 private-GPU card inspected against established field reference and prerequisite chronology. Complete principal heads/actions retained, headless/GPU PASS14 effective bindings across year0..600, hashes, hidden gating and crop bounds.
